question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-not-adopted at queue position 29. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: A Plate table cell holding list paragraphs or several paragraphs serializes under the default lossPolicy reject instead of failing the whole document.
A GFM row stays on one line and every surviving cell keeps its column; no raw line ending or row-splitting pipe is written.
main's released cell format (inline ul, ol start, li, task checkbox, br) reads back, per the serialized-data law in VISION.md.
Features own mappings: List builds list paragraphs, Table owns grid geometry, the optional platejs/markdown runtime owns intrinsic syntax; Core owns the mapping types only.
Markdown parsing stays DOM-free; editors without List keep list HTML in cells literal.
Loss is explicit. Serialization reports anything one line cannot carry under lossPolicy or as a lossy warning.
evidenceReuse: This review reused the 2026-10-03 constraints record's requirements and prior-art comparison, the plan's arena and panel outcomes, and the execution record's proof claims without rerunning them. On the live tree it rechecked the committed cell encoder refusal via git show HEAD, the working-tree cell encoder and decoder calling encodeLine and decodeLine, the public JSDoc of both members, and git status of the plan, decision log and source files. It ran one headless bun probe of serialize and parse against the working tree.
summary: The open job is Markdown fidelity for block content in GFM table cells. A cell may hold list paragraphs and several paragraphs, GFM gives a cell one line of phrasing, and main's released cell HTML must read back. At HEAD fe0e9599a6 the cell encoder refuses non-paragraph blocks and the row refuses a refused cell, so serialize fails under the default reject policy. The working tree adds encodeLine and decodeLine to the Markdown mapping contexts, implemented in markdownLine.ts. That tree is staged, not committed, and another session was still editing it at 01:25 to 01:27 today. A headless probe on that tree serializes a cell list under reject to main's one-line HTML and reads main's released cell back as list paragraphs. The strongest replacement writes the whole table as a raw HTML block when a cell holds blocks, and it loses. It needs an HTML-table reader that the D6 dialect law rejects, and it still has to read main's released cell format under the serialized-data law. Making the lowering a runtime intrinsic on tableCell would delete two public context members, but it forces mappings to emit a non-standard mdast tree, which the decision page already rejects. A Table-private codec cannot reach the optional runtime. Nothing in the design needs reopening. The remaining gap is landing the build. The round 3 fixes are unreviewed (owner question), two frozen benchmark lines missed (owner chose keep), and nothing is committed.

callSites.current: In committed code, editor.api.markdown.serialize({ document }) returns ok false when a table cell holds list paragraphs, because the cell markdown.encode refuses and the row and table refuse in turn; main's cell list HTML parses to literal tag text.
callSites.proposed: In the working tree, built but not committed, editor.api.markdown.serialize({ document }) returns ok true with the cell on one line of inline list HTML. The table cell mapping is encode: ({ encodeLine, node }) => ({ children: encodeLine(node.children), type: 'tableCell' }), and the table decoder reads each cell with decodeLine(cell.children, marks) (proposed public context members).

reconciliation.reason: Its partial outcome and limits stand. The build is in the working tree only, the round 2 and 3 fixes are unreviewed, and two benchmark lines missed with the owner's keep.

alternatives: Keeping the refusal (HEAD) loses. Every export or copy of a document with a list in any cell fails under reject, and the table disappears under allow.

Writing the whole table as a raw HTML block when any cell holds blocks loses. It needs an HTML-table reader inside a CommonMark dialect whose D6 law keeps unregistered raw HTML literal, and the parser must read main's released one-line cell format anyway.

Deleting the two public context members and lowering tableCell children inside the runtime as an intrinsic loses narrowly. Mappings would have to emit tableCell with flow children, a non-standard mdast tree the decision page rejects, and other table mappings lose the helper.
A Table-private codec or HTML-list spelling in Table loses. Table cannot import the optional runtime, and list syntax in Table duplicates List's decode, which is how main's table rules drifted.
Reusing the feature HTML mappings in cells is a Stop per the earlier record. It produces verbose output that breaks GFM rows and adds a DOM requirement on parse.
Pursue the one-line codec behind encodeLine and decodeLine, List-built list paragraphs and grid-aware span flattening (built, uncommitted) to landing.
proofLimits: This is a source review plus one headless bun probe against the working tree, which another session is editing (markdownLine.ts and MarkdownNodeMapping.ts have unstaged changes, and the plan and decision log were modified minutes before this review). This review read HEAD behavior from git show and did not execute it. It ran no package suite, browser copy, github.com rendering or benchmark. It reused the execution record's test and benchmark claims without replaying them. Every decisive fact about the built target rests on uncommitted files.
